questiontext.text: Which connector type does the source of the Lab 3 channel use?

generalfeedback.text: The Lab 3 channel receives messages with a Channel Reader: messages come from other channels or from Send Message, not from the network or a folder.

feedback.text: Correct.
A TCP Listener receives messages over the network. Lab 3 doesn't listen on a port.
A File Reader polls a folder. In Lab 3 you send the HL7 file by hand instead.
The Channel Writer is the destination of the Lab 3 channel, not the source.

questiontext.text: A Channel Reader listens on a network port, so external systems can send messages to it directly.

generalfeedback.text: A Channel Reader only receives messages from inside the same OIE server: from a Channel Writer, from router.routeMessage() or from Send Message.

feedback.text: Not correct: a Channel Reader has no network port.
Correct.

name.text: L3-03 Ways to reach a Channel Reader

questiontext.text: Which of these can send a message to a channel whose source is a Channel Reader? Select all that apply.

generalfeedback.text: A Channel Reader receives from a Channel Writer in another channel, from router.routeMessage() in a script, and from Send Message in the Administrator.

answer.text: A Channel Writer destination in another channel

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

answer.text: Send Message in the Dashboard or Message Browser

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: An external system sending HL7 over MLLP

feedback.text: Not correct: that needs a TCP Listener source.

answer.text: A file copied into a folder on the server

feedback.text: Not correct: that needs a File Reader source.

questiontext.text: In Lab 3, the Channel Writer's Channel Id is set to None. What happens to a message that reaches this destination?

generalfeedback.text: With Channel Id None the message isn't forwarded anywhere. That lets you test the channel without a second channel.

answer.text: It is not forwarded to any other channel.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: It gets status ERROR because there is no target.

feedback.text: Not correct: in Lab 3 the message gets status SENT.

answer.text: It is sent back to the source of the same channel.

feedback.text: Not correct: that would create a loop.

answer.text: The channel can't be deployed until a target is chosen.

feedback.text: Not correct: the channel deploys fine with Channel Id None.

questiontext.text: What is the default Template of a Channel Writer? Type it exactly.

generalfeedback.text: The default template is ${message.encodedData}: the message as this destination encoded it.

feedback.text: Correct.
Not the default: rawData is the original message as received.

generalfeedback.text: In Development mode OIE keeps every version of the message (raw, transformed, encoded, sent, response), so you can inspect all of them in the Message Browser.

answer.text: OIE keeps every version of the message, so you can see them all in the Message Browser.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: It makes the channel process messages faster.

feedback.text: Not correct: storing more content makes processing slightly slower, not faster.

answer.text: A Channel Reader only works in Development mode.

feedback.text: Not correct: a Channel Reader works with any storage mode.
Not correct: encryption is a separate setting.

questiontext.text: You click Deploy Channel. What do you see next?

generalfeedback.text: OIE opens the Dashboard automatically. A newly deployed channel shows status Started with all counters at 0.

answer.text: The Dashboard, with the channel Started and all counters at 0

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: The Message Browser, with one test message already processed

feedback.text: Not correct: deploying doesn't send a message.

answer.text: The Dashboard, with the channel Stopped until you start it

feedback.text: Not correct: the Lab 3 channel's initial state is Started.

answer.text: The channel editor stays open with a "Deployed" message

feedback.text: Not correct: OIE switches to the Dashboard.

questiontext.text: The Deploy Channel option isn't available for your channel. What should you check first?

generalfeedback.text: A disabled channel can't be deployed. In Channels, right-click the channel, choose Enable Channel, and deploy again.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Whether the HL7 test file is in the right folder

feedback.text: Not correct: the test file only matters when you send a message.
Not correct: a Channel Reader doesn't use a port.

answer.text: Whether the Message Browser is open

feedback.text: Not correct: deploying doesn't depend on the Message Browser.

questiontext.text: You send an HL7 test message to the Lab 3 channel and refresh the Message Browser. Which status does Destination 1 show when everything works?

generalfeedback.text: The Channel Writer delivered the message (to nowhere, because Channel Id is None), so the status is SENT.

feedback.text: Correct.
Not correct: the Lab 3 channel has no filter.
Not correct: queuing is off in Lab 3.
Not correct: ERROR means something went wrong.

questiontext.text: Match each tab in the Message Browser with what it shows.

generalfeedback.text: Raw is what came in, Transformed is OIE's internal form after the transformer, Encoded is converted to the outbound data type, and Sent is what the connector actually sent.

answer.text: The message exactly as it was received
The message in OIE's internal form, after the transformer
The message converted to the outbound data type
What the destination connector actually sent

questiontext.text: Because the Lab 3 channel has no filter or transformer steps, the message content is the same in the Raw, Encoded and Sent tabs.

generalfeedback.text: True: without filter or transformer steps, OIE passes the message through unchanged.

feedback.text: Correct.
Not correct: nothing in the channel changes the message.

questiontext.text: You have sent three HL7 test messages to the deployed Lab 3 channel, and all were processed. What do the Dashboard counters show for the channel?

generalfeedback.text: Each message is received once and sent once by Destination 1, so both counters show 3.

feedback.text: Correct.
Not correct: Destination 1 sends every message, even with Channel Id None.
Not correct: the channel has no filter.
Not correct: the counters add up every message.
